title: Detect Squares
keyIdea: Store counts of each point (duplicates matter). For count(x, y), each stored point (px, py) with |px − x| = |py − y| ≠ 0 is a possible opposite corner; the square's other corners are (x, py) and (px, y). Add cnt[px][py] × cnt[x][py] × cnt[px][y].

approaches.name: Count grid + diagonal corner
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). cnt[1001][1001] plus a list of distinct points; count loops over distinct points as diagonals and multiplies the three corner counts.
approaches.space: O(P) for points (+ the fixed 1001 × 1001 grid)
approaches.why: Each count looks at every distinct stored point once (P of them).

quiz.q: Why loop over the diagonal corner instead of a side corner?
options: The diagonal alone fixes the whole square (side length and direction)
Either works the same with less code
Each copy of each corner gives a different square
Zero side length is not a square (positive area required)
